title: Retry-limit and backoff logic
difficulty_rationale: One module, but four interacting defects in control flow (attempt counting, exception filtering, delay capping, re-raising) that must all be fixed without breaking the injected-sleep design.
summary: retry_call() performs one call too many, retries non-retryable exceptions, ignores the backoff cap and hides the original exception.
required_behavior: func is called at most max_attempts times in total (max_attempts >= 1, otherwise ValueError).
Only exceptions that are instances of retry_on are retried; any other exception propagates immediately.
The delay before retry k (k = 1, 2, ...) is min(base * factor**(k-1), max_delay) and is passed to the injected sleep function.
No sleep happens after the final failed attempt.
When all attempts fail, the last exception raised by func is re-raised unchanged.
on_retry, if given, is called as on_retry(attempt_number, exception, delay) before each sleep.
acceptance_criteria: Public API of retrykit is unchanged.

acceptance_tests.description: func is called exactly max_attempts times when it always fails.
Exceptions outside retry_on are not retried.
Backoff delays follow base*factor^(k-1) capped at max_delay.
Sleep is not called after the last attempt.
The final exception object is re-raised unchanged.
on_retry receives attempt number, exception and delay.
